aggregate_method: For each scene and registered case, retain the source summary’s two independent process values and its median separately for P/off, C/off, or C/on/off. Aggregate tables below summarize the six case-level medians (and six per-case ratios) with median/minimum/maximum; they are not pooled event samples.

candidate_recording_on_exact_physical.interpretation: Candidate-only recording-on supports exact physical-gap tails. P/off tails are not equivalent exact physical-tail evidence; the registered comparison says reference/off samples cannot certify these tails.

input_response_observation.interpretation: Only three of 72 cases contain an observed upward-pose response: two P/off and one C/off repetition of Wave512 near-material-fire-on; no response sample exists for the paired C/on trials or other cases. This is insufficient for a general input-response comparison.

residual_findings: Mixed2048 candidate/off input admission regresses: median of six case-level medians is 180.880 ms versus 155.357 ms for P/off (+16.4% on these aggregate medians; median per-case C/P ratio 1.220).
Mixed2048 candidate/off per-case request latency reaches a 381.850 ms case median for scene-replacement despite being lower than the matching P/off value; replacement remains a visible latency tail.

Candidate recording-on exact physical-gap p95 and maximum targets (100 ms and 250 ms) are missed in both scenes. Worst per-case p95 is 119.642 ms in Wave512 and 265.780 ms in Mixed2048; worst maximum is 1,222.193 ms and 4,384.192 ms respectively.
The hosted software-renderer process/draw observations do not establish owner-hardware responsiveness or physical scanout.
